text:
andrea: heads-up — I saw a noticeable tail-latency regression on /v1/generate-hosted around 23:12 UTC last night. p99 per-token went up ~2.5x. dashboard: https://graf.redwood/yr/generate-hosted (see token-latency breakdown)
perf-bot: ALERT automated: route=/v1/generate-hosted p95_token_latency=312ms (baseline 115ms), p99_token_latency=840ms, kvcache_hit_rate=0.62, avg_queue_wait_ms=38.4, kernel_fallback_rate=0.18
jamal: interesting — do we have the batch_size histogram and kernel_selector counts for that window? looks like fallback triggers when batch_size crosses a threshold. can we get a quick PromQL?
keiko: pulled the trace samples — most slow requests hit the fallback path (nv_ff32 fallback) and show spikes in `cudaMemcpy` + `kernel_launch` latency. flamegraph attached (summary): memcopy ~32%, kernel_launch_wait ~41% when fallback used.
andrea: here's a PromQL I ran for the 23:00-23:30 window: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket{route="/v1/generate-hosted"}[5m])) by (le))` and `sum(rate(kernel_selector_fallback_total{route="/v1/generate-hosted"}[5m])) by (instance)` — both jump at ~23:12.
jamal: can you paste the query you used for kvcache? want to check hit vs eviction rate. also check queue_wait vs seq_len distribution.
keiko: kvcache info: `kvcache_hit_ratio{route="/v1/generate-hosted"}` dropped from ~0.9 to 0.62 around the same time; eviction_delta spiked correspondingly. looks like longer queue waits let active prefixes expire from LRU window on some nodes.
keiko: quick config idea — lower the kernel switch threshold and add a soft gate on batcher when avg_queue_wait_ms > 50ms to avoid chasing fallback kernels. patch suggestion:
```yaml
runtime:
  kernel_selection:
    kernel_switch_threshold: 96 # was 128
  batcher:
    soft_queue_wait_limit_ms: 50
    max_batch_wait_ms: 12
```
jamal: lgtm as a short-term mitigation. we should also emit `kernel_fallback_rate`, `per_route_kvcache_hit_ratio`, and `batcher_avg_queue_wait_ms` to the per-route KPI dashboard. add p50/p95/p99 batch_size histograms too.
andrea: I'll own the canary. plan: open PR with the two small runtime config changes + dashboard tiles, roll a canary to 10% capacity on dedicated pool in us-west-2, monitor p95/p99 token latency and kvcache_hit_ratio for 30m. cc @keiko for flamegraph follow-ups. :crossed_fingers:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: runtime-configs:v2026.03.18-canary1 -> cluster-us-west-2 (10%) starting in 30m. health-checks: p95_token_latency, kvcache_hit_ratio, kernel_fallback_rate.
jamal: also add an alert: fire if kernel_fallback_rate > 0.1 for 5m AND p99_token_latency > 600ms.
andrea: will add that to the PR description. PR will reference tracing snapshots and include the flamegraph. opening PR now (will post link). thanks all.
keiko: if the canary looks good we should follow up with a longer-term fix: revisit kernel-selection heuristics and consider keeping a tiny hot-kvcache guard to avoid premature eviction during queue spikes.
andrea: noted. follow-up ticket created: infra/ENGRT-4467 (kernel-selection + kvcache guards).
